title: Lev Vidmar explains what science allows regarding time travel
excerpt: Physicist Lev Vidmar explains that science allows travel to the future according to Einstein's relativity, while travel to the past remains speculative. Quantum teleportation, already demonstrated, transfers state information, not matter or people.
content:
The physicist Lev Vidmar, from the Jožef Stefan Institute and the University of Ljubljana, reviews in an interview released by Svet na Kanalu A what science currently allows regarding time travel and where its limits still lie. He distinguishes travel to the future, supported by Einstein's relativity, from travel to the past, still speculative, and clarifies that quantum teleportation, already demonstrated, transfers state information, not matter or people.

Relativity, quantum teleportation and three-dimensional air traffic 🚀

Einstein's relativity supports travel to the future through time dilation, an effect measured in high-precision clocks and in accelerated particles. Travel to the past, on the other hand, lacks a technological basis and remains in the realm of speculation. Quantum teleportation, already demonstrated in the laboratory, transfers state information between particles, not matter or people. Flying vehicles, for their part, would require managing traffic in three dimensions. Artificial intelligence and quantum computers appear as tools for finding new physical patterns.

Travel to the past is still waiting for its first volunteer ⏳

While relativity gives us a one-way ticket to the future, travel to the past continues without a technological basis and without a departure date. Quantum teleportation transfers state information, so no one should expect to materialize in the office without dealing with traffic. And if flying vehicles ever arrive, traffic will have to be managed in three dimensions: the fine for excess altitude promises to be historic.
